To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the energy overhead of DSDV is independent of the transmission radius, (2) the energy overheads of AODV and DSR are proportional to the transmission radius squared, (3) the energy overhead per hop is higher for AODV than for DSDV and for DSR than for AODV, and (4) the energy overhead increases with the transmission power at an exponential rate for all three protocols.

(1) DSDV consumes the least amount of energy when the transmission range is small; however, it consumes the largest amount of energy when transmission range is large, (2) DSR is the most efficient protocol in terms of the number of routing messages, (3) DSR consumes the most energy, and (4) AODV is in the middle in terms of energy consumption.

the routing overheads of DSDV and AODV are very different and depend in non-trivial ways on the transmission radius, while the routing overheads for DSR are almost constant and independent of the transmission radius.

the routing energy overhead of the DSR protocol decreases as the transmission radius increases, whereas the overhead of the DSDV protocol increases with the transmission radius and that of the AODV protocol is fairly constant.
the DSR protocol is the most power-efficient for small networks and low traffic, but AODV is the best for larger networks and high traffic.
the DSR protocol has the least energy overhead when the transmission power is small (less than 10 dBm) and the DSDV protocol has the least overhead when the transmission is large (larger than 10 dB).
The main takeaway from our work is that

the energy overhead is an important metric to consider when evaluating the routing protocols for mobile ad-hoc networks, and it is not sufficient to simply use the number of packets as a metric for the overhead.
the energy overheads of the protocols are quite different from each other, and the differences can be significant.
it is important to study the energy overhead of a routing protocol as a function of the transmission power, since it can vary significantly with it.
